item.content:encoded:
Window: 09 Sep 18:00 → 09 Sep 22:00 UTC (4 hours)

Cisco confirms CVE-2026-20079 Secure FMC flaw exploited in attacks — Must Read

Cisco confirmed that a critical Secure Firewall Management Center authentication bypass flaw, CVE-2026-20079, is being actively exploited to gain root-level command execution. Customers should urgently apply Cisco’s fixes, as there are no workarounds and patching will not clean up already compromised devices.

  • Cisco confirmed that CVE-2026-20079, a maximum-severity authentication bypass vulnerability in Secure Firewall Management Center software, is being actively exploited in attacks.
  • The flaw has a CVSS score of 10.0 and can allow unauthenticated remote attackers to execute scripts and commands as root on vulnerable devices by sending crafted HTTP requests to the web interface.
  • Cisco says there are no workarounds and recommends that customers upgrade to the latest software release, while warning that hot fixes will prevent future exploitation but will not remediate already compromised devices.
  • CISA added CVE-2026-20079 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and ordered Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies to secure vulnerable systems by September 12, 2026.
  • Indicators published in July, including a log entry involving /var/tmp/license.tmp dated July 23, suggest the flaw may have been exploited before Cisco said its PSIRT became aware of active exploitation in August.

Technologies: firewall

Products: cisco-secure-firewall-management-center, cisco-security-cloud-control-firewall-management

Vendors: cisco

AdaptHealth confirms 4.1 million people exposed in July cyberattack — Must Read

AdaptHealth confirmed that a June cyberattack exposed personal and health-related data for 4,115,802 people after attackers used social engineering to compromise a privileged third-party contractor account. The incident has been attributed to ShinyHunters, though AdaptHealth says it has not found evidence of stolen data being misused.

  • AdaptHealth confirmed that data belonging to 4,115,802 individuals was exposed in a cyberattack discovered in July.
  • The company said the compromise occurred on June 5 after a social engineering ploy compromised the privileged account of a third-party contractor.
  • The exposed data may have included full names, contact information, demographic information, health insurance information, and health information.
  • An unnamed threat actor contacted AdaptHealth on June 15 to demand a ransom payment in exchange for not leaking the stolen data.
  • HIPAA Journal previously reported that ShinyHunters was responsible for the attack, but BleepingComputer could not find an AdaptHealth entry on ShinyHunters’ extortion portal.

U.S. Disrupts Xinbi Guarantee Scam Marketplace, Freezes $52.8 Million in Crypto — Should Read

U.S. authorities disrupted the Xinbi Guarantee scam marketplace by seizing Telegram channels and crypto wallets and freezing $52.8 million tied to scam laundering. The action targets a major Telegram-based ecosystem used by organized crime groups to support pig-butchering scams and global scam compounds.

  • The U.S. Department of Justice announced coordinated actions against Xinbi Guarantee, including seizing Telegram channels, confiscating two cryptocurrency wallets, and deploying the Scam Center Strike Force to Madagascar.
  • Authorities froze $52.8 million in cryptocurrency from 52 wallets associated with Xinbi Guarantee and its merchant network, bringing the Scam Center Strike Force’s total restrained funds to about $938 million.
  • Elliptic said Xinbi Guarantee is the second-largest illicit marketplace of its kind, with $30 billion in transactions since around 2022, and helped the U.S. Secret Service identify and freeze wallets holding $52.8 million in Tether’s USDT.
  • Xinbi Guarantee acted as an intermediary between vendors and scam center operators by holding payments until services such as scam investment websites, money laundering, and recruitment for scam compounds were completed.
  • The Justice Department said the Scam Center Strike Force helped take down 13 scam centers in Madagascar, where more than 3,200 electronic devices were seized and investigations were opened after interviews with nearly 400 arrestees.

Products: telegram, usdt, tron, usdd, xinbi-guarantee

Vendors: telegram, tether, tron-dao, elliptic

Skullcandy Dime 3 earbuds expose users to Bluetooth hijacking — May Read

Skullcandy Dime 3 earbuds running firmware 1.0.0.28 can be silently paired by nearby attackers due to CVE-2025-20701, enabling audio hijacking and microphone access. Although Skullcandy says firmware 1.0.0.30 fixes the issue, existing users currently have no consumer-accessible way to update vulnerable units.

  • CERT/CC warned that Skullcandy Dime 3 wireless earbuds accept Bluetooth pairing requests from nearby unpaired devices without requiring user interaction.
  • Skullcandy Dime 3 devices running firmware version 1.0.0.28 are affected by CVE-2025-20701, a high-severity missing-authentication vulnerability in the Airoha Bluetooth Audio SDK.
  • An attacker in close range can connect without a pairing PIN, physical access to the earbuds case, or an approving pairing request, and can later interrupt the owner’s connection, hijack audio playback, access the headset profile, and capture live microphone audio.
  • Skullcandy says the issue was fixed in firmware version 1.0.0.30, but CERT/CC says users with existing vulnerable units currently have no consumer-accessible method to update them.
  • CVE-2025-20701 was discovered by ERNW researchers, presented at the TROOPER cybersecurity conference, and affects a broad range of earbud and headphone products from multiple vendors.

Technologies: iot-device

Products: skullcandy-dime-3, airoha-bluetooth-audio-sdk, beats-studio-buds

Vendors: skullcandy, airoha, apple

Grindr settles privacy lawsuit tied to disclosure of users’ HIV statuses for $35 million — May Read

Grindr agreed to pay about $35 million to settle a UK privacy lawsuit alleging it shared sensitive user data, including HIV status, with advertisers before 2020. The company denies liability and says it has since overhauled its privacy practices under new ownership.

  • Grindr agreed to pay £26 million, or $35.2 million, to resolve a UK lawsuit alleging it provided advertisers with sensitive user data, including users’ HIV status.
  • The settlement will be paid in two lump sums, with one payment due by the end of December and the other due by the end of March, according to a September 4 SEC filing.
  • The lawsuit was filed by UK users in April 2024 and concerned alleged privacy law violations from before early 2020, when Grindr was owned and run by the Chinese company Kuntun.
  • Grindr’s regulatory filing said the settlement includes no findings or admission of liability, and the company disputes the allegations.
  • Grindr’s then chief privacy officer said in May 2024 that the company never used users’ health-related information for advertising purposes and that information was shared with two service providers to support a profile feature.

CISA head says agency must change quickly to prevent the 'worst that could happen' — Optional

CISA acting director Nick Andersen warned that the U.S. faces potentially devastating cyber risks from years of poor decisions, technical debt, staffing shortages, and AI-driven threats. He said the agency must rapidly rebuild its workforce and make major changes to avoid failing to prevent the worst outcomes.

  • CISA acting director Nick Andersen warned that Americans face significant and possibly devastating cybersecurity vulnerabilities due to past government mistakes, overwhelming technical debt, outdated technology, and AI threats.
  • Andersen said CISA must make serious and significant changes quickly or risk failing to prevent what he described as the worst that could happen.
  • Andersen said CISA has about 250 incoming staff who have been screened and hired and are waiting for security clearances.
  • CISA lost about a third of its staff after DOGE-related cuts and attrition during the first year of the Trump administration.
  • The agency is prioritizing hiring for its operational, cybersecurity, infrastructure security, and emergency communications divisions, as well as regional field workers.

Silent Push 6.1: Built to Get There First — Optional

Silent Push released platform version 6.1, led by a new brand and infrastructure impersonation detection engine designed to spot look-alike domains and attacker infrastructure before campaigns launch. The update also adds faster investigation workflows and integrations with SOAR, browsers, AI agents via MCP, and STIX/TAXII feeds.

  • Silent Push Platform 6.1 introduces a next-generation Brand and Infrastructure Impersonation engine designed to detect look-alike domains during the preparation phase before attacks are weaponized.
  • The new impersonation detection engine can surface look-alike domains, score them by risk, enrich them with registrar, hosting, and page-title context, cluster them by associated threat actor, and notify teams on a schedule as new candidates appear.
  • Silent Push 6.1 adds investigation workflow improvements including My Assets, Advanced Pivot Control, expanded Insight Search, and Total View enhancements such as a PADNS timeline, IP certificates, one-click PDF export, and screenshot date filtering.
  • The release adds integrations for Palo Alto Cortex XSOAR, a Chrome Extension, an MCP server for AI assistants and agentic workflows, and an updated bidirectional TAXII Server for STIX/TAXII threat-intelligence exchange.
  • Platform 6.1 adds support for custom analyst reports with TLP: AMBER+STRICT and provides localized interfaces in Korean and Spanish alongside English, with Japanese coming soon.

item.title: Chrome CVE-2026-87491 Exploited; SAP, cPanel, F5 and Defender Flaws Escalate Risk
item.content:encoded:
Window: 09 Sep 06:00 → 09 Sep 10:00 UTC (4 hours)

Chrome V8 Zero-Day Exploited in the Wild Enables Code Execution Inside Sandbox — Must Read

Google patched an actively exploited Chrome V8 zero-day, CVE-2026-87491, that could let a remote attacker run code inside Chrome’s sandbox via a crafted HTML page. Users should update Chrome to the latest fixed versions immediately, and Chromium-based browsers should apply fixes when available.

  • Google released Chrome updates to patch 230 security vulnerabilities, including CVE-2026-87491, which has been exploited in the wild.
  • CVE-2026-87491 is a medium-severity out-of-bounds write bug in Chrome’s V8 JavaScript and WebAssembly engine that can allow a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code inside the sandbox via a crafted HTML page.
  • Security researcher Jihyeon Jeong of Compsec Lab at Seoul National University reported CVE-2026-87491 to Google on August 6, 2026, and received a $2,500 bug bounty reward.
  • The update also fixes five critical flaws in WebGL and Cast components, including use-after-free, out-of-bounds write, and buffer overflow issues.
  • Users are advised to update Chrome to versions 153.0.8010.36/.37 for Windows and macOS and 153.0.8010.36 for Linux, while users of other Chromium-based browsers should apply fixes when available.

Technologies: browser

Products: google-chrome, v8, webgl, google-cast, microsoft-edge, brave-browser, opera-browser, vivaldi-browser

Vendors: google, microsoft, brave-software, opera, vivaldi-technologies

SAP Patches CVSS 10.0 Kernel Flaw Enabling Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution — Must Read

SAP released urgent patches for several critical flaws, including a CVSS 10.0 SAP Kernel Extended Passport bug that allows unauthenticated remote code execution with SAP admin privileges. Organizations should prioritize patching exposed SAP systems because standard SAP access controls cannot mitigate the pre-authentication attack path.

  • SAP released security updates for multiple vulnerabilities, including CVE-2026-44756, a CVSS 10.0 memory corruption flaw in SAP Extended Passport Processing.
  • CVE-2026-44756, codenamed OVERPASS by Onapsis, is remotely exploitable without authentication and can allow attackers to run arbitrary operating system commands on the SAP host with SAP administrative privileges.
  • Onapsis said OVERPASS is reachable through several SAP components and communication protocols, including the internet-facing web layer, SAP GUI layer, and RFC layer.
  • SAP also patched CVE-2026-58240, a CVSS 9.8 missing authentication check in SAP NetWeaver Message Server that Onapsis named S4GET.
  • Onapsis recommended that users inventory every SAP system, patch internet-facing systems before internal instances, reduce exposure where possible, and monitor for exploitation attempts.

Products: sap-kernel, sap-extended-passport, sap-netweaver-message-server, sap-cloud-application-programming-model, sap-netweaver-sap-gui-for-java, sap-s4hana, sap-s4hana-cloud-private-edition

Vendors: sap, onapsis

F5 BIG-IP APM Malware Injects a PHP Web Shell Into Memory, Evading Disk Scans — Must Read

Sophos found that malware tied to exploited F5 BIG-IP APM systems can inject a PHP web shell into Apache/PHP memory without changing the on-disk scripts, allowing it to evade normal file scans. Defenders should investigate even patched appliances, checking memory, modified binaries, logs, and F5 integrity signals for compromise.

  • Sophos said malware linked to break-ins at F5 BIG-IP Access Policy Manager appliances hides a PHP web shell in memory instead of storing it as a file on disk.
  • The malware injects the web shell into Apache’s in-memory copy of apm_css.php3, full_wt.php3, or webtop_popup_css.php3, so disk checks of those scripts can appear clean.
  • F5 linked the c05d5254 activity to CVE-2025-53521, a BIG-IP APM flaw it reclassified on March 27, 2026 as unauthenticated remote code execution that had been exploited.
  • Sophos said an installer sample named umount infects /usr/sbin/httpd by adding malicious code to the front of the real Apache web server file.
  • Defenders are advised to investigate patched systems for prior compromise using signals such as sys-eicheck failures, modified /usr/bin/umount or /usr/sbin/httpd files, suspicious logs, HTTP 201 CSS responses, and memory-versus-disk differences.

Technologies: load-balancer, vpn, remote-access, web-server

Products: big-ip-apm, apache-http-server, php, icontrol-rest, selinux, qkview, sys-eicheck

Vendors: f5, sophos, eset, apache-software-foundation

New cPanel Flaw Lets a Hosting Account With Mail Privileges Run Code as Root — Must Read

cPanel patched CVE-2026-67401, an EmailTrack SQL injection flaw affecting all supported cPanel/WHM versions that could let an authenticated hosting account with mail privileges create files and execute code as root. Admins should upgrade to the fixed builds immediately, though cPanel has not provided mitigations or guidance for checking prior compromise.

  • cPanel patched CVE-2026-67401, an SQL injection flaw in EmailTrack that can let an authenticated account holder with mail-related privileges create files on the server and run code as the root user.
  • cPanel said every supported version of cPanel and WHM is affected and named fixed builds for release lines 11.110, 11.134, 11.136, 11.138, and WP Squared.
  • The advisory does not explain how the SQL injection leads to file creation and root access, and it does not provide temporary mitigation steps for servers that cannot update immediately.
  • cPanel also does not say whether installing the patched build helps a server that was attacked before the update or how an administrator would check for prior compromise.
  • As of September 9, no public exploit code or exploitation report for CVE-2026-67401 appeared in searches, and the flaw was absent from CISA’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog released September 8.

Products: cpanel-whm, emailtrack, wp-squared

Vendors: cpanel

New Microsoft Defender 'ShieldCrash' zero-day grants SYSTEM access — Must Read

A researcher released a new Microsoft Defender zero-day called ShieldCrash that can grant SYSTEM-level arbitrary file read on fully patched Windows systems, claiming Microsoft’s September patch failed to fully fix the earlier ShieldBreak flaw. Microsoft had not yet commented or released an official fix.

  • An anonymous security researcher known as Nightmare Eclipse released a new Microsoft Defender zero-day exploit named ShieldCrash after Microsoft issued its September 2026 Patch Tuesday security updates.
  • Nightmare Eclipse described ShieldCrash as a bypass for the ShieldBreak Defender privilege escalation flaw that Microsoft patched as CVE-2026-69414.
  • The ShieldCrash proof-of-concept exploit is said to allow attackers to gain SYSTEM privileges on fully patched Windows 10, Windows 11, and Windows Server systems, but not write access.
  • Nightmare Eclipse said the proof of concept demonstrates arbitrary file read as SYSTEM on all supported Windows versions with the September 2026 updates installed.
  • Microsoft was not immediately available to comment when BleepingComputer asked about the ShieldCrash zero-day.

Technologies: antivirus, operating-system

Products: microsoft-defender, windows-10, windows-11, windows-server, bitlocker

Vendors: microsoft

Man gets 15 years for extorting women with AI-generated porn videos — May Read

An Ohio man was sentenced to 15 years in prison for cyberstalking and sextortion after using AI tools to create and share explicit deepfake images and videos of victims, including child sexual abuse material. He is the first person convicted under the new Take It Down Act, which bans nonconsensual explicit AI forgeries and revenge porn.

  • An Ohio man, James Strahler II, was sentenced to 15 years in prison for cybercrimes including sextortion and cyberstalking of numerous victims through phone calls, voicemails, text messages, and online posts.
  • Court documents said Strahler used more than 100 AI web-based models and more than 24 AI platforms to generate sexually explicit videos and images of his victims.
  • The Justice Department said Strahler sent harassing messages to at least six adult female victims from December 2024 until June 2025, including nude images that were both real and AI-generated.
  • Strahler pleaded guilty in April to cyberstalking, producing obscene visual representations of child sexual abuse, and publication of digital forgeries charges.
  • The article says Strahler was the first defendant convicted of violating the Take It Down Act, a 2025 law prohibiting online publication of explicit content and AI forgeries without consent.

Active exploitation of Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center vulnerabilities — Must Read

Cisco Talos warns that two Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center vulnerabilities, including a critical authentication bypass, are being actively exploited by state-sponsored and ransomware actors. Organizations should apply Cisco’s hotfixes immediately and investigate for signs of web shells, reverse shells, Cyclops Blink malware, and Qilin-related activity.

  • Cisco Talos is tracking active exploitation of CVE-2026-20079, a critical authentication bypass vulnerability in Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center Software, and CVE-2026-20316, a static-credentials vulnerability that allows remote login with a low-privileged account.
  • Cisco says hotfixes are already available for affected software versions and strongly advises customers to apply them immediately, with a broader hardening release planned for the week of September 14 or September 16 as stated in the article.
  • Talos identified a UAT-12197 activity cluster in which attackers exploited CVE-2026-20079 to deploy a JSP web shell, place a malicious cmd.jar command executor, and query internal databases for user authentication data and credentials.
  • Talos attributes a UAT-11823 cluster to an advanced persistent threat actor overlapping with Sandworm tooling, involving exploitation of the vulnerabilities, Netcat-based reverse shells, configuration exfiltration, and deployment of a Cyclops Blink variant.
  • Talos also describes UAT-11988 as a ransomware operator that used CVE-2026-20316 static credentials to access an FMC device, conduct reconnaissance and credential theft, create tunnels into the victim network, and later deploy Qilin ransomware on selected endpoints.

Four Spy Groups Used the Same Chrome and Windows Exploit Kit Within a Week — Must Read

Multiple espionage groups, mostly suspected China-linked, rapidly adopted a new BlueMoon exploit kit chaining Chrome V8 and Windows ALPC flaws to compromise targets via phishing links. Patching Chrome and Windows blocks the initial exploit path, but organizations that may have been targeted should also hunt for persistence and payload artifacts such as GemStone, ShadowPad, suspicious scheduled tasks, and temp-folder executables.

  • Proofpoint reported that multiple espionage-motivated threat activity clusters used a previously undocumented exploit kit called BlueMoon within days of its first observed in-the-wild use by APT31 on August 28, 2026.

  • The attacks began with phishing emails that led victims to actor-controlled URLs serving BlueMoon, after which the kit downloaded different payloads depending on the threat cluster, including GemStone, ShadowPad, Rust malware, and DLL sideloading components.
  • Observed targets included U.S. non-governmental organizations, mining companies, physical commodity trading firms, U.S. aerospace companies, a Vietnamese manufacturing entity, and government, consulting, and financial sector organizations in Indonesia and Singapore.
  • Proofpoint said updating the browser closes the initial access route but does not remove already installed artifacts such as the GemStone extension, scheduled tasks, files in the Windows TEMP folder, or related registry and mutex indicators.

AdaptHealth confirms 4.1 million people exposed in July cyberattack — Must Read

AdaptHealth confirmed that a June cyberattack exposed personal and health-related data of 4,115,802 people after attackers used social engineering to compromise a third-party contractor’s privileged account. The company says affected individuals are being offered 12 months of free credit monitoring and has found no evidence of data misuse so far.

Unit 42 uncovered CL-CRI-1171, a pay-per-install operation using YouTube gaming content and SEO-poisoned software downloads to spread a generic loader called OfferLoader. The key risk is that seemingly routine commodity loader infections can hide multiple serious payloads, including Insomnia RAT, ARKTunnel and Docro Hijacker.

  • Unit 42 tracks the activity as CL-CRI-1171, a pay-per-install operation that has operated under the radar for at least two years and provides an infection service for other threat actors.
  • CL-CRI-1171 used at least two delivery funnels: gaming-focused YouTube channels and SEO-poisoned search results leading to trojanized software downloads.
  • Unit 42 identified more than 10,000 distinct OfferLoader samples and more than 200 rotational domains following a distinctive two-word compound naming pattern across several top-level domains.
  • In April 2026, OfferLoader delivered three separate malware families in two intrusion sets: Insomnia RAT, ARKTunnel and Docro Hijacker.
  • Unit 42 identified 11 YouTube channels tied to CL-CRI-1171 that collectively had hundreds of thousands of subscribers and millions of views, and YouTube terminated the channels after being notified.

CVE-2026-75650, a critical unauthenticated RCE zero-day in Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source dubbed StyleSmuggler, has been actively exploited since September 4 before Adobe released a hotfix on September 7. Hackers breach F5 BIG-IP APM devices to deploy Linux rootkit — Must Read

Attackers are compromising F5 BIG-IP APM devices, likely via CVE-2025-53521, to deploy a Linux rootkit that injects a fileless PHP web shell into memory and avoids leaving malicious files on disk. Defenders should patch affected systems and look for signs such as unusual POST requests to targeted .php3 files, HTTP 201 CSS-like responses, and Apache processes altering libphp memory or spawning bash.

  • A Linux rootkit targeting F5 BIG-IP APM environments can intercept PHP file loading and inject a fileless web shell directly into memory without writing malicious code to disk.
  • Sophos researchers said the malware appears to be a second-stage payload likely deployed after exploitation of CVE-2025-53521, a critical remote code execution flaw in F5 BIG-IP.
  • The implant hooks Apache and PHP-related loading mechanisms, targets BIG-IP APM webtop PHP files such as apm_css.php3, full_wt.php3, and webtop_popup_css.php3, and leaves the PHP files on disk unchanged.
  • The injected web shell accepts specially formatted requests, decrypts their contents, executes them through PHP’s eval() function, and returns an HTTP 201 response disguised as CSS content.
  • Sophos said defenders should look for signs such as Apache workers reading /proc/self/maps, changes to libphp memory protections, creation of /run/bigtlog.pipe, launches of /bin/bash, and unusual POST requests to the targeted .php3 endpoints.

SAP patched two critical vulnerabilities, including the maximum-severity OVERPASS flaw in SAP Kernel that could let unauthenticated or low-privileged attackers remotely execute commands and fully compromise exposed SAP systems. CrowdStrike says a previously undocumented Brazil-based threat actor, Slim Spider, has been targeting Brazilian financial institutions to steal cloud credentials and cryptocurrency custody secrets, with a focus on Pix and digital asset infrastructure. FreeIPA Flaw Chain Lets Anonymous Clients Create Reusable Administrator Credentials — Must Read

Red Hat disclosed a critical FreeIPA flaw chain that can let anonymous clients create reusable administrator credentials on default installs by abusing a 389 Directory Server access-control bug. FreeIPA 4.13.4 and related 389-ds updates address the issue, while admins without fixes should restrict LDAP access or disable anonymous binds where possible.

  • The FreeIPA issue becomes exploitable through a second flaw in 389 Directory Server, CVE-2026-76560, where an unauthenticated client with an empty name can match an empty stored owner value in an access-control rule.
  • The FreeIPA project fixed its side of the issue in version 4.13.4, while Red Hat published multiple 389-ds advisories on 8 September and had not yet listed fixed ipa packages for Red Hat Enterprise Linux when checked.
  • Red Hat also disclosed a separate FreeIPA flaw, CVE-2026-79678, in which the idp-add command passes user-supplied values into a Python eval() call before the permission check, allowing any account on the server to read environment variables one at a time or consume server memory.

A massive fake e-commerce network called DoppelCart is using more than 119,000 cloned shop domains to steal shoppers’ payment card details and personal information in real time. Over 105,000 of the sites remain active, impersonating more than 44,000 brands with steep discounts to lure victims.

  • A fraud operation dubbed DoppelCart uses more than 119,000 domains to run fake e-shops that steal payment card details.
  • Nebty said more than 105,000 DoppelCart shops are still active, and 96% of confirmed shops share identical build files and resolve to 27 commerce backends.

Cisco Talos uncovered a ClearFake ClickFix campaign that uses Cloudflare Workers, BNB Smart Chain-hosted JavaScript, and WebDAV to deliver Amatera stealer to Windows victims, including a Ukrainian government organization. Amatera then deploys ZigCryptoStealer, a reverse proxy, or unauthorized NetSupport Manager remote-access software, with one branch assessed as likely operated by a Russian threat actor.

A CIA official said the agency’s Cyber Mission Center enabled cyber operations that built the intelligence picture used to locate and capture Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro. He also said AI is expected to increasingly shape CIA cyber, collection, operations, and analysis work.

Compromised Flutter package on pub.dev contains XCSSET malware — Should Read

A Flutter package on pub.dev, universal_file_viewer version 0.1.5, was accidentally published with XCSSET malware after the maintainer’s Mac was infected.   • The package’s Dart library code in lib/ is clean, and the infected files are in the example/ directory, so simply adding universal_file_viewer as a dependency does not trigger the malware.

French prosecutors confirmed the arrest of an 18-year-old suspected ZeroBytes member accused of participating in cyberattacks on France’s tax authority and other organizations. Singaporean national Malone Lam pleaded guilty to RICO conspiracy charges for leading the Social Engineering Enterprise, a group accused of stealing more than $245 million in cryptocurrency through social engineering, remote access scams, and physical thefts. Italian privacy-focused tech collective Autistici/Inventati says it will shut down after the U.S. designated it a terrorist organization, triggering sanctions risks, domain suspension, and loss of banking access. Token Analysis and Tracking System (TATS) — Should Read

TATS is an open-source tool for collecting, decoding, and visualizing OAuth token exchanges, with special support for Microsoft cloud behaviors like brokered client IDs and FOCI. It can steal browser data and cookies, hijack sessions, manage files, and maintain persistence by tampering with Chromium settings and policies.

JSCeal Malware Can Bypass Google Authentication Using Stolen Session Cookies — Should Read

JSCeal is an actively developed malware campaign targeting crypto traders through fake trading sites and malicious ads, stealing browser cookies, passwords, OAuth tokens, and other data. Researchers found it can replay stolen Google session cookies to bypass authentication and also intercept or modify traffic for cryptocurrency services like Binance, Bybit, and Ledger.

  • Check Point Research analyzed JSCeal, a compiled V8 JavaScript malware protected with javascript-obfuscator techniques including RC4-protected strings, control-flow flattening, proxy functions, and operation wrappers.
  • JSCeal is distributed through fake cryptocurrency trading sites reached via malicious ads on Facebook and Google, where users are instructed to download bogus TradingView installers.
  • The malware can enumerate installed Chromium-based browsers and extract cookies, saved passwords, OAuth tokens, and other data from browser profiles.
  • JSCeal can use stolen cookie data to reconstruct browser sessions and conduct active session replay attacks to bypass authentication and access victims’ Google accounts.
